steps.title: Prepare basic reagents
steps.instruction: Make 10 % (v/v) TCA, 90 % and 100 % acetone, and a 10 mM MM(PEG)24 stock solution, keep them cold and store appropriately.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 % (v/v) trichloroacetic acid (TCA) and keep at 4 °C before use.
Prepare 90 % acetone (v/v) in water, cool at –20 °C; also prepare 100 % acetone and keep at –20 °C.

Dissolve methyl‑maleimide polyethylene glycol [MM(PEG)24] to 10 mM in dimethylformamide (DMF) or dimethyl‑sulfoxide (DMSO), aliquot to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles and store at –20 °C in a moisture‑free condition.

steps.title: Make 1× lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Combine the listed reagents to obtain a final volume of 50 mL of lysis buffer and store at 4 °C; add protease inhibitor cocktail just before use.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL of 1 M Tris (pH 7.5) to give 50 mM Tris.
Add 1.5 mL of 5 M NaCl to give 150 mM NaCl.
Add 0.25 mL of 2 M MgCl₂ to give 10 mM MgCl₂.
Add 5 mL glycerol (10 %).
Add 1 mL of 0.5 M EDTA to give 1 mM EDTA.
Add 0.5 mL of 0.1 M PMSF to give 1 mM PMSF.
Add water to bring the volume to 50 mL.
Store at 4 °C; keep PMSF and protease inhibitor cocktail at –20 °C and add 1× protease inhibitor cocktail immediately before use.

steps.title: Make 1× resuspension buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the resuspension buffer (50 mL) containing SDS, urea, glycerol, SDS, bromophenol blue and Tris; use freshly added urea and store at 4 °C to 25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 6.25 mL of 400 mM Tris (pH 7.5) to give 50 mM Tris.
Add 12.01 g urea (4 M final concentration).
Add 1 mL glycerol (2.5 %).
Add 1 g SDS (2 %).
Add 2.5 mg bromophenol blue (0.005 %).
Add water to a final volume of 50 mL.
Store at 4 °C–25 °C; add fresh urea each time the buffer is prepared.

steps.title: Make 1× SDS‑PAGE running buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of running buffer containing Tris, Glycine and SDS; store at 4 °C to 25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 30.28 g Tris to obtain 250 mM (final 25 mM) in water.
Dissolve 142.63 g Glycine to obtain 1.9 M (final 190 mM) in water.
Add 10 g SDS to give a 1 % stock; dilute to 0.1 % final concentration.
Add water to bring the total volume to 1 L.
Store at 4 °C–25 °C.

steps.title: Make 1× transfer buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of transfer buffer with Tris, Glycine and 20 % methanol; add methanol just before use and store at 4 °C to 25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 30.28 g Tris (250 mM stock) and 142.63 g Glycine (1.9 M stock) in water.
Add 200 mL methanol to obtain 20 % (v/v) methanol.
Add water to a final volume of 1 L.
Store at 4 °C–25 °C; add methanol immediately before use.

steps.title: Make 1× TBS‑T buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of Tris‑buffered saline with Tween 20 (TBS‑T) and store at 4 °C to 25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 8.5 g Tris (400 mM stock) to give 20 mM Tris.
Dissolve 1.75 g NaCl (3 M stock) to give 150 mM NaCl.
Add 1 mL Tween 20 to obtain 0.1 % (v/v).
Add water to a final volume of 1 L.
Store at 4 °C–25 °C.

steps.title: Make 1× stripping buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 30 mL of stripping buffer containing Tris, SDS and β‑mercaptoethanol; add β‑mercaptoethanol just before use and store at 4 °C to 25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 0.57 g Tris (0.5 M stock) to give 62.5 mM Tris (pH 6.8).
Add 3 mL of 2 % SDS.
Add β‑mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 100 µM (add fresh before use).
Add water to a final volume of 30 mL.
Store at 4 °C–25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare blocking solution
steps.instruction: Make freshly 1 % (w/v) non‑fat dry milk in TBS‑T for antibody incubation.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g non‑fat dry milk in 100 mL TBS‑T.

steps.title: Generate oxidized and reduced controls
steps.instruction: Grind frozen tissue, extract protein with lysis buffer, then treat aliquots with CuCl₂ or DTT to obtain oxidized and reduced controls.

substeps.instruction: Grind frozen biological material and aliquot 20 mg into 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 90 µL lysis buffer, vortex, and incubate on ice for 15 min.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 15 min; transfer supernatant to a new tube.
For oxidized control: add 10 µL CuCl₂ (300 µM stock) to reach 30 µM final; incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
For reduced control: add 10 µL DTT (400 mM stock) to reach 40 mM final; incubate at 37 °C for 75 min.
Store oxidized and reduced samples at –20 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Extract proteins and label thiols
steps.instruction: Precipitate proteins with cold TCA, wash pellets with acetone, resuspend, and conjugate reduced cysteines with MM(PEG)24.

substeps.instruction: Grind fresh biological material in liquid nitrogen and aliquot 20 mg into 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 1 mL cold 10 % (v/v) TCA to each sample (including oxidized/reduced controls) and vortex immediately.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 16,000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 1 mL cold 90 % acetone, vortex, centrifuge at 11,000 g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Repeat wash with 1 mL cold 100 % acetone, centrifuge as above, discard supernatant.
Dry pellet at 37 °C for 5 min (do not over‑dry).
Resuspend pellet in 90 µL resuspension buffer.
Add 10 µL of 10 mM MM(PEG)24 (final 1 mM).
Incubate at 65 °C for 5 min, then at 22–25 °C for 1 h to allow alkylation.
Store labeled samples at 4 °C for up to one week (prefer fresh use).

steps.title: Run non‑reducing SDS‑PAGE and blot
steps.instruction: Separate proteins by non‑reducing SDS‑PAGE, transfer to a membrane, and block with milk solution.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a non‑reducing SDS‑PAGE gel using the running buffer prepared earlier.
Load the MM(PEG)24‑treated samples (and controls) without reducing agents.
Run electrophoresis at the appropriate voltage until the dye front reaches the bottom.
Equilibrate the gel in transfer buffer and assemble the transfer sandwich.
Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose or PVDF membrane using the transfer buffer (20 % methanol) at the recommended current/time.
After transfer, block the membrane with the 1 % milk/TBS‑T solution for the recommended time.

steps.title: Detect and analyze blot
steps.instruction: Develop the western blot using ECL, expose to X‑ray film, and quantify band intensities.

substeps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of ECL solution A and B (≈2–3 mL total for a 12 cm × 6 cm membrane).
Remove excess buffer from the membrane without letting it dry.
Place the membrane in a tray, add the ECL mixture, and incubate at 22–25 °C for 0.5–5 min.
Remove excess ECL solution.
Wrap the membrane in plastic wrap inside an X‑ray film cassette.
Expose the cassette to X‑ray film in a dark room for seconds to hours, depending on signal strength.
Develop the film using a processor (e.g., Konica medical film processor) or manually.
Measure band intensities with image analysis software (e.g., ImageJ).
Normalize each band to a housekeeping protein (e.g., Actin) and calculate relative intensities compared with the control.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for detection of reduced or oxidized status of protein cysteine-thiols. We have used this protocol to determine the redox state of Thioredoxin like 1 (TRXL1) protein in plants grown under normal condition or subjected to abiotic and biotic stress for various time points (Pant et al., 2020). Oxidation-reduction of regulatory proteins and metabolic enzymes containing cysteine thiols leads to formation or breakage of disulfide bond causing changes in protein conformation, folding, monomerization or oligomerization or complex formation (Chung et al., 2013; Rouhier et al., 2015; Waszczak et al., 2015). Protein thiol redox modification alters protein activity, stability and redox signaling cascades in cell under normal condition or in response to various factors such as diurnal, environmental and developmental cues (Brandes et al., 2009; Finkel, 2011; Putker and O'Neill, 2016). Timing: 2–3 days
